adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/compatibility/CompatibilityResult.java:34 — Exit code 4 changes from "recreate required" to "feature disabled" and recreate moves to 3, so existing automation keyed on 4 silently misreads results and 3 falls into an unhandled branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the meaning of exit code 4 in `CompatibilityResult` (from `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4` to `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and moves recreate-required to exit code 3. The CLI commands also now call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `rolling-updates` is not enabled. This is a clear externally observable contract change for tooling/automation consuming exit codes; the diff itself doesn’t show it’s a functional defect inside Keycloak, but it is a backward-incompatible behavior change that likely needs explicit communication/migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:49 — testFeatureNotEnabled only covers metadata and checks just the message, never the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code or the check subcommand, so a wrong exit code would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: In UpdateCommandDistTest, the new testFeatureNotEnabled runs only `UpdateCompatibility` + `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` (no `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`) and asserts only the error text via `cliResult.assertError(...)` without asserting the process exit code. Given the diff introduces a new exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and explicitly calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` in both `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()`, this test does not verify the new behavior fully; an incorrect exit code (or incorrect handling in the check subcommand) could still pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:53 — The macro appends a hardcoded --features=rolling-updates after the user's parameters, so a user who already passes --features=... gets a duplicate/overriding option and may drop their real features, making metadata/check run against a different config than the deployment.

adjudication.rationale: In docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc the updatecompatibility macro was changed to always append `--features=rolling-updates` after `${parameters}` (`bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ${parameters} --features=rolling-updates`). This can lead to duplicated `--features` options if `${parameters}` (or a user copying the command and adding their own flags) already contains `--features=...`, which is at least confusing and may change which features are actually enabled depending on CLI option precedence. The diff doesn’t show the CLI option parsing semantics, so the claimed “drops their real features” outcome can’t be fully verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/compatibility/CompatibilityResult.java:34 — Exit code 4 was the shipped "recreate required" code and now means "feature disabled" (recreate moved to 3), so existing callers that key on 4 will silently misread results.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, while new command logic exits with `FEATURE_DISABLED` when the feature is off (`picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata`). This is a real, diff-grounded backwards-compatibility concern for any external scripts/callers that previously interpreted exit code `4` as “recreate required”. However, the diff does not show any in-repo callers that still key on `4`, so it’s not verifiable as an internal functional bug from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:53 — Documented command appends `--features=rolling-updates`, which replaces rather than adds to the user's configured `features` list, so the metadata/check runs against a different feature set than the real deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows docs template `kc.adoc` changing the command to include `--features=rolling-updates` (and related code that requires the feature to be enabled). It does not show how the `--features` CLI option is parsed/merged with any existing feature list, so the claim that it "replaces rather than adds" (and therefore checks a different feature set than the real deployment) cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — New feature-disabled test checks only the message, not the new public exit code 4, and doesn't cover the `check` subcommand.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` (added around lines 46-52) only asserts the error message via `cliResult.assertError(...)` and does not assert the exit code, even though the diff introduces a new public exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and explicitly calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` in both `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()`. Also, the feature-disabled scenario is only exercised for the `metadata` subcommand via `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})`; there is no analogous test invoking `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME` without `--features=rolling-updates` to cover the same gating logic in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:115 — setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) overwrites any features already enabled on the test deployment instead of appending rolling-updates

adjudication.rationale: In UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment, the diff unconditionally calls `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`, which replaces the entire enabled-features list rather than merging/appending. The diff does not show whether `createBasicKeycloakDeployment()` (or other setup) already populates enabled features, so the claim about overwriting existing enabled features cannot be fully verified, but the overwrite behavior is real and could make the test less robust if features were preconfigured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error message and never asserts the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new dedicated exit code for disabled feature (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` explicitly call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled. The new test `testFeatureNotEnabled` (UpdateCommandDistTest.java) only asserts the error message and does not assert the exit code, so it doesn’t verify the newly added nontrivial behavior (exit code signaling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:47 — Feature-disabled path is only tested for the metadata subcommand; the new guard in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is untested.

adjudication.rationale: In UpdateCommandDistTest, the new feature-disabled behavior is exercised only via `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})` in `testFeatureNotEnabled`, which hits the guard added in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`. All tests that invoke the `check` subcommand (e.g., `testMissingOptionOnCheck`, `testCompatible`, `testWrongVersions`) pass `ENABLE_FEATURE`, so the guard added in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (`if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) ...`) is never covered by a test in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:97 — RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, but the incompatible tests assert only messages, not the exit code, so the contract change goes unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 (`quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java`). In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the “wrong versions”/incompatible-path assertions only check error text (e.g., `result.assertError(...)`) and do not assert the non-zero exit code for the recreate/incompatible outcome, unlike `testCompatible` which asserts `exitCode()==0`. So the changed exit-code contract is not directly verified by these tests in the shown diff.
